title: Pressing down: Fodor's lemma and the Δ-system lemma

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 63–65 (Lemma 14.15, Definition 15.1 and Lemma 15.2; root bounds and closure function corrected)

summary: Pressing down fixes a stationary fiber and organizes uncountably many finite sets around a common root.
abstract: Sending each successor ordinal to its predecessor gives a function with no repeated values, even though it always lowers its argument. Fodor's lemma says that a function sending each ordinal to a smaller one must be constant on a stationary subset, if its domain is stationary in a regular uncountable cardinal. Here stationary means meeting every closed unbounded set. An application shows that every uncountable family of finite sets has an uncountable subfamily with one fixed pairwise intersection, called a delta-system. For finite assignments of zeros and ones, fixing both the common overlap and its values gives an uncountable subfamily whose assignments agree wherever they overlap.
